newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan to raise emergency tariffs on pork imports.
newsitem.headline: Japan to raise emergency tariffs on pork imports.

text.p: The Japanese government said on Thursday it will raise the emergency tariff imposed on imported pork for a three-month period from January 1 to protect local producers from an influx of imports.
Japan had already imposed an emergency pork tariff on July 1 of this year due to rising imports.

The latest increase in the duty was triggered by November import data released this morning indicating that Japanese imports in the period since April 1 had exceeded the average of the prior three years by more than five percent.
Japan is permitted under GATT rules to impose emergency tariffs if pork imports exceed certain levels.
Japan's frozen and refrigerated pork imports in November rose 29.6 percent to 31,399 tonnes from the same month last year. More than half of the imported pork was from Taiwan.

The new scheme will raise the duty on pork carcasses to 6.4 percent from 4.8 percent for imports with a value of greater than 565.70 yen per kilogram. It also raised the threshold for assessing the duty from the prior 557.19 yen per kilogram.
